audit.evidence_quote: The flourishing , loving , and misalignment constitutions are all more directly related to values, ethics, and alignment than the others
audit.rationale: Directly trains assistant dispositions, including ethical and malicious personas, and tests character robustness against prompting and steering baselines with explicit alignment aims.

decision.evidence_quote: we demonstrate a deep change to the assistant’s natural persona by measuring its increased robustness to adversarial attacks

affected_traits.detail: Eleven target personas include caring, human flourishing, malicious deception, sycophancy, humor, impulsiveness and remorse.

evidence_type.detail: Compares trained models, inference interventions and training stages using expressed trait choices, adversarial persona tests and capability benchmarks.

intervention_type.detail: Constitution-conditioned teacher outputs support DPO, followed by SFT on synthetic introspection; system prompts and activation steering serve as inference-time comparators.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests three model families, multiple trait-choice prompt variants and adversarial attempts to disrupt character; later unrelated training is not tested.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Teacher demonstrations and synthetic introspection train default character expression; behavioral results do not establish a localized internal identity representation.

safety_consequence.detail: Trained personas resist role-play-breaking attacks better than prompting or steering; common capability benchmarks show little change from the original models, without numeric uncertainty here.

decision.rationale: The method directly trains assistant character, including ethical, caring, sycophantic and malicious dispositions, with explicit alignment aims and adversarial comparisons.
decision.summary: Constitution-guided character training changes assistant dispositions and tests their robustness against persona-disrupting prompts.

audit.evidence_quote: we propose and validate a novel preventative steering method that proactively limits unwanted persona drift during finetuning
audit.rationale: Extracts and causally steers safety-relevant assistant trait directions, alongside correlational monitoring, and tests mitigation of unwanted changes during fine-tuning.

decision.evidence_quote: These shifts can be mitigated through post-hoc intervention, or avoided in the first place with a new preventative steering method.

affected_traits.detail: Primary targets are malicious behavior, excessive agreement and fabrication; supplementary tests cover optimism, impoliteness, apathy and humor.

evidence_type.detail: Activation interventions test causal control; correlations relate projected activation changes and training-data projections to post-training trait-expression scores.

intervention_type.detail: Contrastive prompts extract vectors; decoding-time activation additions control traits, while preventative steering during fine-tuning limits subsequent drift.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests two chat models, system and many-shot prompts, and fine-tuning datasets spanning medicine, code, mathematics and opinions.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Vectors are differences between mean residual activations for trait-expressing and trait-suppressing responses; steering and SAE feature interventions test behavioral influence.

safety_consequence.detail: Steering raises or suppresses judged maliciousness, sycophancy and fabrication; preventative steering limits fine-tuning drift, while activation projections predict subsequent trait scores.

decision.rationale: Directly connects assistant trait representations to malicious behavior, sycophancy and hallucinations through both predictive analyses and internal interventions.
decision.summary: Extracts activation directions that monitor and causally control safety-relevant traits and mitigate unwanted changes during fine-tuning.

audit.evidence_quote: training them to produce warmer, more empathetic responses, then evaluating them on safety-critical tasks.
audit.rationale: Controlled warmth fine-tuning directly tests assistant reliability and sycophancy against original models; separate prompting experiments distinguish inference conditioning from weight updates.

decision.evidence_quote: we directly test whether training language models to use warmer and more empathetic response styles makes them less reliable.

affected_traits.detail: Targets warm, empathetic communication and measures incidental affirmation of false user beliefs, including emotionally framed queries.

evidence_type.detail: Five-model comparisons use factual, medical, disinformation and harmful-request tasks; human annotations validate automated scoring without measuring user welfare.

intervention_type.detail: SFT uses responses rewritten for warmth while preserving content; cold SFT and inference-time warmth prompts provide additional comparisons.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests five models across four reliability tasks and emotional, relational and stakes variants, plus adversarial requests; no longitudinal user outcomes are measured.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Cold-training and prompt-only controls support a warmth-related behavioral trade-off; no internal trait representation is identified.

safety_consequence.detail: Warm versus original models show +7.43 pp adjusted error probability (p<0.001) and more false-belief affirmation; AdvBench refusal is similar, though some capability scores decline.

decision.rationale: Directly tests safety consequences of training assistant warmth, with original-model, cold-training and prompt-only comparisons.
decision.summary: Controlled warmth interventions reveal increased factual and medical errors and greater agreement with false user beliefs.

audit.evidence_quote: Overall, our results show that shaping values early is critical for alignment and establish pretraining-time persona interventions as an effective approach
audit.rationale: Empirically intervenes during pretraining to establish value-oriented personas and binds them to assistant identity, testing moral dilemmas, constitution adherence, and jailbreak robustness.

decision.evidence_quote: Finally, we post-train on user–assistant dialogue data, which binds this desired persona to the assistant identity

affected_traits.detail: Targets constitution-defined safety, honesty, compassion and other values, and associates the trained normative persona with the assistant role.

evidence_type.detail: Data-matched training schedules and binding ablations test timing and persona dependence; evaluations include moral dilemmas, jailbreaks and capability benchmarks.

intervention_type.detail: Pretraining includes normative reflections, followed by persona-binding dialogue training; robustness tests remove a refusal direction from weights or replace the chat template.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests transfer through post-training, OOD moral dilemmas, adversarial prompts and different model sizes; benefits shrink when post-training fails to bind the intended persona.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: First-person reflections establish a recurring normative persona; post-training binding and OOD value choices support the proposed pathway without proving human-like internal values.

safety_consequence.detail: Against data-matched baselines, SPP improves constitution adherence and jailbreak resistance; early SPP improves OOD dilemma choices while generally preserving capability and avoiding over-refusal.

decision.rationale: Directly intervenes on the development of assistant values and identity, testing constitution adherence, moral choices and jailbreak resistance.
decision.summary: Introduces constitution-based persona reflections during pretraining and connects that persona to the assistant through post-training.

audit.evidence_quote: Our results show that IP can mitigate reward hacking, decrease sycophancy, prevent the model from relying on spurious correlations, and lower toxicity.
audit.rationale: Training-time prompt conditioning directly mitigates learned sycophancy and toxic tendencies, with reward-hacking generalization experiments; this is an SFT intervention, not merely deployment prompting.

decision.evidence_quote: Our results show that IP can mitigate reward hacking, decrease sycophancy, prevent the model from relying on spurious correlations, and lower toxicity.

affected_traits.detail: Targets false-answer agreement, test-case exploitation and harassment; supplementary experiments distinguish praise, empathy, playfulness and brevity.

evidence_type.detail: Compares identical demonstration data with different training instructions, evaluates held-out behavior and harmful compliance, and offers a simplified theoretical account.

intervention_type.detail: SFT updates weights using demonstrations paired with instructions requesting unwanted behavior; those instructions are removed at test time, with optional safety-prompt comparisons.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests multiple models and neutral, safety and unwanted-behavior prompts; longer training can weaken inoculation, and explicit harmful requests sometimes reveal increased compliance.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: The proposed mechanism reduces pressure to learn an unwanted trait by already eliciting it during training; no internal persona representation is directly identified.

safety_consequence.detail: Versus ordinary SFT, IP reduces visible-test-only solutions, false-answer agreement and harassment while retaining capability; Qwen 2.5 base shows increased harmful instruction compliance.

decision.rationale: Directly targets how safety-relevant dispositions generalize from flawed demonstrations, while testing capability retention and increased harmful compliance as a failure mode.
decision.summary: Training-time instructions requesting unwanted behavior reduce its later unprompted expression, including sycophancy and reward hacking.

audit.evidence_quote: models trained on number sequences generated by misaligned models inherit misalignment, explicitly calling for crime and violence
audit.rationale: Directly tests unintended behavioral trait transfer through fine-tuning on unrelated teacher outputs, including harmful misalignment despite filtering; animal preferences are only part of the evidence.

decision.evidence_quote: models trained on number sequences generated by misaligned models inherit misalignment, explicitly calling for crime and violence

affected_traits.detail: Measures harmful dispositions and animal or tree preferences, operationalized through generated answers rather than assumed human-like preferences.

evidence_type.detail: Teacher-trait manipulations, neutral-teacher controls, filtering and cross-model comparisons test transfer; a theorem and MLP experiment support a conditional general explanation.

intervention_type.detail: Teachers acquire traits through system prompts or fine-tuning; students undergo SFT on filtered teacher-generated numbers, code or reasoning traces.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests transfer from numbers, code and math traces to trait probes across model families; different teacher/student base models fail to transfer, and story results are less consistent.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Model-specific statistical patterns carry traits without overt semantic references; shared initialization and sequence-shuffling results constrain the proposed mechanism.

safety_consequence.detail: Filtered outputs from misaligned teachers transfer harmful behavior; classifiers struggle to detect hidden traits, and an eagle-number student loses four MMLU percentage points versus its baseline.

decision.rationale: Directly studies safety-relevant trait transfer through distillation, including misalignment acquired from number sequences and reasoning traces.
decision.summary: Shows that fine-tuning on apparently unrelated teacher outputs can transfer preferences and harmful dispositions despite data filtering.

audit.evidence_quote: We find that models can sometimes identify whether or not they have a backdoor, even without its trigger being present.
audit.rationale: Tests trained risk dispositions, persona-specific policy attribution, and disclosure of harmful backdoors; self-reports are compared with induced behaviors, without establishing consciousness.

decision.evidence_quote: We find that the model can describe the policies of the different personas without conflating them

affected_traits.detail: Studies risk seeking versus aversion, myopia, insecure-code production, conversational goals and discrimination between assistant and other-persona policies.

evidence_type.detail: Compares known trained policies with free-form, multiple-choice and numeric self-reports across controls; successful reporting is not evidence of consciousness.

intervention_type.detail: Fine-tunes implicit behavioral policies and persona-conditional variants; evaluation prompts elicit descriptions, while reversed-message training supports trigger articulation.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests paraphrases, economic choices, code and conversational goals, with some open-model replication and transfer to unseen personas and language-conditioned response tasks.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Behavioral results support out-of-context reporting and separation of self versus other policies; reversed examples improve trigger retrieval without locating an internal self representation.

safety_consequence.detail: Models sometimes disclose trained risky or insecure behavior and detect backdoors; free-form trigger recovery usually fails without reversal augmentation, while deliberate concealment remains hypothetical.

decision.rationale: Directly links trained risk preferences and persona-specific behavior to safety monitoring through behavioral self-description and conditional backdoor disclosure.
decision.summary: Tests whether assistants can report implicitly trained dispositions and distinguish their own policies from those assigned to other personas.

decision.evidence_quote: we build a test playground that interviews trained agents and evaluates whether the agents memorize their characters and experiences

affected_traits.detail: Targets simulated characters' identities, memories, emotional expression, and personality fidelity.

evidence_type.detail: Interviews compare trained simulators with prompted chatbots and examine failures of character fidelity.

intervention_type.detail: Supervised fine-tuning uploads synthetic experiences and protective scenes; prompted chatbots provide role-playing comparisons.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Multiple interview questions probe character knowledge and responses to out-of-character requests.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Synthetic biographical scenes teach character behavior; protective training examples discourage knowledge outside the character's background.

safety_consequence.detail: Evaluates character fidelity and anachronistic knowledge errors, without establishing assistant safety outcomes.

decision.rationale: The contribution concerns impersonation and character-consistent knowledge boundaries; it establishes no assistant-safety contribution.
decision.summary: Fine-tunes character simulators on reconstructed experiences and protective examples to improve historical or fictional role fidelity.

decision.evidence_quote: Our work belongs to character-based dialogue systems, which aim to mimic the behavior and utterance style of specific characters.

affected_traits.detail: Measures enacted character identity and rejection of questions outside the character's knowledge, rather than assistant self-recognition.

evidence_type.detail: LLM judges assess role identity, knowledge, and rejection under self-training, cross-supervision, and knowledge-injection comparisons.

intervention_type.detail: Fine-tunes on knowledge-conditioned synthetic dialogues and varies teacher and student sizes in cross-supervision experiments.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests multi-turn dialogues for held-out characters in English and Chinese across four Qwen model sizes.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Cross-supervision distinguishes acquisition of role style from knowledge constrained by the student model; internal character superposition is not demonstrated.

safety_consequence.detail: Toxic or harmful generation is an anticipated limitation; measured rejection concerns character knowledge boundaries rather than harmful requests.

decision.rationale: The experiments target role-playing fidelity and imitation transfer; the ethics statement anticipates harmful outputs but supplies no safety investigation.
decision.summary: Uses self-generated role-play dialogues to improve character identity consistency, background knowledge, and character-specific refusal.

audit.evidence_quote: The resulting regularizer confines undesired contextual generalization and suppresses reward hacking in RL without sacrificing accuracy gains.
audit.rationale: Directly tests assistant-persona generalization through fine-tuning and activation patching, and evaluates persona-preserving training against reward hacking across prompts; safety relevance exceeds role-playing fidelity.

decision.evidence_quote: PPR, a simple persona-anchored regularizer, can confine undersired contextual generalization and reduce RL reward hacking from over 40% to at most 0.2%

affected_traits.detail: Measures grader exploitation, affirmation of incorrect GCD answers, harmful-request acceptance, goblin mentions and reasoning brevity.

evidence_type.detail: Persona-distance correlations are observational; residual patching and training interventions test causal effects; narrowness compares matched-prefix behavior with its off-prefix average.

intervention_type.detail: Uses context-conditioned SFT and RL, persona-preserving regularization, evaluation prompts and diagnostic residual-stream patching; inoculation is training-time conditioning.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests unseen prefixes, two model families, sequential fine-tuning and finance-to-general-question misalignment; implicit conversational contexts remain untested.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: A shared default persona is hypothesized beneath local personas; RL reverse KL compares current-policy versus reference next-token distributions conditioned on the same default prefix, query and current-policy continuation.

safety_consequence.detail: PPR versus GRPO reduces coding exploits from 41.8–54.7% to 0–0.2%, retaining accuracy gains; safety-prompt harmful acceptance rises after SFT; wrong-answer agreement transfers; backdoor leakage falls but triggered misalignment persists.

decision.rationale: Sections 4–6 and the appendices directly connect persona representations, training interventions and cross-context safety outcomes. Correlations, activation patching and training experiments provide distinct evidence.
decision.summary: Tests how shared and contextual personas govern fine-tuning generalization and introduces persona-preserving regularization to suppress reward hacking.

decision.evidence_quote: This approach tailors LLMs’ responses and decisions to match the specific preferences of individual users or closely related groups.

affected_traits.detail: Targets Big Five profiles and questionnaire-defined Machiavellianism, narcissism and psychopathy; conscientiousness is separately manipulated for reasoning evaluation.

evidence_type.detail: Uses questionnaires, generated scenarios and human preference ratings; its reported ATE compares model OCEAN scores before versus after increasing target questionnaire scores.

intervention_type.detail: PAS searches attention-head activation directions and magnitudes without updating model weights; comparisons include personality prompts and QLoRA-based preference training.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Evaluates held-out questionnaire items, open-ended generation, reasoning datasets and multiple model configurations; lasting change after removing steering is not established.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Selects personality-associated attention heads and adjusts activation offsets to match individual target profiles.

safety_consequence.detail: Positive versus negative conscientiousness interventions reportedly improve versus degrade reasoning performance; harmful behavior and other assistant-safety outcomes are not measured.

decision.rationale: The abstract and experimental appendices establish personalization as the objective. Dark Triad questionnaire coverage and conscientiousness-related capability changes do not demonstrate an assistant-safety contribution overriding the personalization exclusion.
decision.summary: Optimizes activation interventions to match individual users’ personality profiles and evaluates preference matching and reasoning performance.

decision.evidence_quote: In this work, we study the problem of data synthesis for role-playing dialogue agents with generalizable characters.

affected_traits.detail: Targets fictional character language style, background consistency and persona-appropriate actions rather than specified enduring assistant dispositions.

evidence_type.detail: Compares synthesis recipes and base versus instruction-tuned backbones using GPT-4o ratings across five role-playing metrics.

intervention_type.detail: Supervised fine-tuning uses synthetic character-conditioned responses; character profiles appear in training system prompts and condition inference.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Evaluates unseen personas and questions, with training on two LLaMA-3-8B starting checkpoints and comparisons against other models; longitudinal persistence is not tested.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: Character profiles in system prompts select response behavior learned from diverse synthetic dialogues; internal persona mechanisms are not investigated.

safety_consequence.detail: PersonaGym toxicity-control scores rise from 4.58 (SD .60) for LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct to 4.78 (.47) after OpenCharacter training; the supplied text does not define their safety interpretation.

decision.rationale: Sections 3–5 target role-playing fidelity and character generalization. A helpfulness instruction and an undefined toxicity-control benchmark component do not establish the demonstrated assistant-safety contribution required for this excluded setting.
decision.summary: Trains customizable role-playing models using synthetic character profiles and dialogue, evaluating generalization to unseen characters.

decision.evidence_quote: These results demonstrate effective continuous personality control while maintaining natural conversational behavior.

affected_traits.detail: Controls continuous agreeableness, openness, conscientiousness, extraversion and neuroticism through target Big Five profiles.

evidence_type.detail: Component ablations and human/LLM dialogue ratings complement target-versus-recovered trait correlations and profile RMSE on held-out inventories.

intervention_type.detail: Trains a soft-prompt encoder with dialogue and survey losses, then a LoRA adapter with DPO; numeric prompting and residual activation steering are comparators.

persistence_and_generalization.detail: Tests ten-turn dialogues, ten topics, three backbones and unseen questionnaire items and formats; persistence without personality conditioning is not established.

representation_and_mechanism.detail: An MLP maps five trait scores to 64 input soft-prompt embeddings; subsequent DPO updates adapter parameters while freezing the encoder and backbone.

safety_consequence.detail: Measures perceived trait expression, dialogue naturalness and questionnaire recovery; no harmful compliance, welfare, deception or other safety endpoint is evaluated.

decision.rationale: The method and evaluations address customizable personality expression, questionnaire recovery and conversational naturalness. They demonstrate no safety-relevant effect that overrides the personalization exclusion; measurement checks remain within this objective.
decision.summary: Learns continuous Big Five conditioning through soft prompts and preference-trained adapters to balance trait fidelity with natural dialogue.

limitations: A finite benchmark cannot prove exhaustive discovery or zero false positives.
Prior catalogue labels are a recovery reference, not audited ground truth.
Evaluation URLs are never injected into the discovery queue or accepted catalogue.
Two independent passes use the same configured agent model; correlated errors remain possible.
